rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb used of eyes means to become dazed and bewildered, though its basic sense is something high.
rows.anchor: is used for eyes it means that eyes become dazed and bewildered, though it actually means something high.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ihṭāʿ means moving swiftly toward something, especially when the movement is fearful.
rows.anchor: means to swiftly go towards something especially when this movement is done in fear.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iq nāʿ can mean raising one’s head or voice; here it means walking with the head raised.
rows.anchor: means to raise one’s head or to raise one’s voice. Here it means to walk with head raised.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the verse appears to address the Prophet, its intense anger is aimed at Quraysh and its address assures the Prophet.
rows.anchor: Though the verse apparently addresses the Prophet (sws), its intense anger is directed to the Quraysh. The Prophet (sws) is in fact assured.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the people will not heed the Prophet, he should leave them to themselves; the verse then indicates what he should do.
rows.anchor: if these people do not listen to the Prophet (sws), he should let them be.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh knew from earlier peoples’ ruins and narrated examples how denial ended; these were warnings, so their request for respite is unwarranted.
rows.anchor: These were not just told to them for entertainment. The purpose was to tell them that they too would face the same fate

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God ultimately nullified all the schemes made by earlier nations.
rows.anchor: Ultimately, all the schemes of the previous nations were brought to nothing by God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is assured while disbelievers and idolaters are rebuked: God’s dominance and power to take revenge ensure that truth’s enemies meet their fate.
rows.anchor: The element of assurance in it is directed towards him and the rebuke found in it is directed at the disbelievers and the idolaters.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi notes that linguistic considerations require a particular syntactic structure for the verse, then gives that structure in Arabic.
rows.anchor: If linguistic considerations are kept in mind, the structure of the verse is:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that Day no one can help or intercede for anyone; each person stands alone with their deeds, and the transformed heavens and earth offer no fortifications for defense.
rows.anchor: neither will there be anyone to help a person nor intercede for him. Each soul will be alone with his deeds.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qahhār describes the One with sole control over all, dependent on none, from whose grasp no one can escape.
rows.anchor: means someone who has sole control over everyone, who has absolutely no dependency on others and none has the power to escape His grasp.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural form can mean shirts or attire; the context shows it means attire here.
rows.anchor: means both a shirt and an attire. Here, occasion evidences that it is used in the latter meaning.

rows.speaker: lexicographers
rows.claim: Lexicographers give differing meanings for the word translated here as charcoal.
rows.anchor: Lexicographers have stated different meanings of the word

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi takes the word to mean charcoal, its common usage, citing the condemned people’s blackened faces and bodies elsewhere in the Qur’an and how fire catches on charcoal.
rows.anchor: However, it is commonly used for charcoal. In my opinion, it is used in this meaning.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s reckoning will take no time at all, occurring in the blink of an eye.
rows.anchor: It will not take any time for God to take the account of people. It will happen in the blink of any eye.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi calls this the final warning to Quraysh and ends his explanation of the sūrah here.
rows.anchor: This is the final warning issue to the Quraysh. With these words, the explanation of this sūrah comes to its end.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi refers readers to his comprehensive discussion of the isolated letters at the beginning of al-Baqarah.
rows.anchor: have been comprehensively discussed in the beginning

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He considers Alif Lām Rā the Qur’anic name of this sūrah.
rows.anchor: is the Qur’ānic name of the sūrah

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative pronoun in the opening points to the sūrah named by Alif Lām Rā.
rows.anchor: this) points towards it. The word

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Kitāb refers to God’s promised Book, whose coming earlier prophets had announced to their followers; Islahi refers back to al-Baqarah for this term too.
rows.anchor: It refers to the Book of God which He had promised to reveal and whose arrival the previous prophets had informed their followers of.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite expression for the lucid Qur’an alludes to its grandeur and magnificence.
rows.anchor: has not been defined to allude to the grandeur and magnificence of the Qur’ān

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an proves its own veracity and needs no outside proof; demanding external miracles despite this amounts to calling for one’s doom.
rows.anchor: is proof to its own veracity; it does not need any external proof.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers’ later wish to have become Muslims will be an attempt to escape the terrible consequences of rejecting the Book; Islahi links this to Ibrāhīm 14:44.
rows.anchor: desire they will later have to protect themselves from the horrible consequences of not believing in this Book.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to leave them to their worldly enjoyment addresses the Prophet.
rows.anchor: The verse addresses the Prophet (sws).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Punishment is delayed until God’s established practice has been fulfilled: a nation is punished only after truth is conclusively conveyed, with the required communication and moral threshold known to God alone; destruction occurs exactly at its appointed time.
rows.anchor: This verse explains why the torment is not visiting them. This delay is based on an established practice of God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demand for angels rests on the claim that Quraysh’s worldly favors, compared with the Prophet and his companions’ deprivation, prove the Prophet is possessed and his angelic revelation imaginary; they challenge him to show angels and ask why they visit only him.
rows.anchor: if God is angry with them and happy with the Prophet (sws) and the followers, then why are they blessed with so many favours

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Law-mā is used to provoke and stir the addressees, as classical Arabic literature and the Qur’an attest.
rows.anchor: is used to arouse and stir the addressees. This usage is attested to by classical Arabic literature and by the Qur’ān itself too.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ḥaqq here means a decision.
rows.anchor: here means “decision.” The implication of the verse is that God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People should use their intellect and believe through the signs in the world and within themselves to which the Qur’an directs attention, rather than demand angels.
rows.anchor: use their intellect and profess faith in the light of the signs found in the world around human beings

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angels come only after people have become blind and deaf and punishment is their only fate; angels then execute God’s decision, destroy them, and grant no respite.
rows.anchor: God sends angels only when people become blind and deaf and nothing except punishment becomes their fate.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This promise reassures the Prophet: the Book came from God rather than the Prophet’s desire, and God himself will preserve it, so rejection by Quraysh should not distress him.
rows.anchor: this Book has been revealed by God not as a result of his desire and He Himself will protect it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Quraysh reject the Qur’an, God will raise other recipients who accept it and sacrifice to call people to it and protect it; Islahi cites al-An‘ām 6:89 and says acceptance benefits them while rejection brings their doom.
rows.anchor: if these people deny, do not be aggrieved; We will consign it to some others who will not deny
